method.description: Tier membership is derived from EXECUTION EVIDENCE, not from source inspection. The full 380-file default suite was run twice: once normally, once with every external endpoint redirected to closed port 59999. Suites that pass normally but fail with endpoints closed genuinely require those services.
method.liveSystemImpact: NONE — process-local env overrides only. No service stopped, no config file edited, no database altered.
method.discardedHeuristic: An earlier static scan estimated 69 non-hermetic files. Spot checks found 3 of 3 sampled were false positives (global.fetch stubbed, a match inside a comment, and jest.mock(http)). That estimate was discarded, NOT refined. The measured figure is 26, established by socket-level enforcement.

socketGuardRun.note: Third and definitive measurement. The env-redirect run (14) was an UNDERCOUNT because several suites hardcode 54322/54321/11434 and never read the redirected variables. tests/tier1-hermetic-guard.js enforces at the socket layer instead and found 12 more. 8 further suites ATTEMPT a blocked connection but still pass — they handle refusal gracefully and are hermetic in outcome, so they remain Tier 1.

tier1_hermetic_unit.description: Runs with every external service unavailable. This is the fast development gate.
tier1_hermetic_unit.enforcement: The tier1 npm script itself redirects PG/Supabase/Ollama to a closed port, so a test that starts needing a service fails loudly instead of silently depending on a developer's running Docker.

tier2_local_service.description: Requires local Postgres and/or the local Supabase REST stack. Measured, not assumed.
tier2_local_service.note: 73 of the 83 migration tests are NOT here. They read migration SQL and assert on its contents, which needs no database. Only these 10 open a connection.

tier3_integration.description: Operational integration suite exercising real OperatorSession/HYDIContinuousRuntime instances against temp data directories.

tier4_qualification.description: Standalone main()-style tsx programs. Slow by design (one is a 500-cycle soak); several expect a live local runtime.
tier4_qualification.note: Named test-*.ts (prefix). That is correct for a main() program and was deliberately NOT renamed; what was missing was a command.

tier5_external.description: Adversarial scripts requiring live SUPABASE_URL / SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. Not run by any gate.

packages_node_test.description: protoforge/packages/* — node:test format, no package.json, previously unreachable by any runner. NOT obsolete: api/platform/{applications,capabilities,dependencies,events}.js import this code.
packages_node_test.knownFailure: protoforge/packages/certification/tests/certifier.test.js:50 'certifies Resonate' — certify('rezonate') returns ok=false. A real application-level drift between the certifier and the rezonate manifest, surfaced by giving these tests a runner. Left red deliberately rather than fixed inside a test-infrastructure phase.

subproject_own_runner.description: Sub-projects with their own test runners. Reachable from their own directory, not from root.

before..githooks/pre-push: npm test  (380 suites, required live Postgres/Supabase)

after..githooks/pre-push: npm test -> tier 1 only, endpoints closed
after.tools/verify.ps1: npm test -> tier 1 only, endpoints closed
after.rationale: A fast gate that silently requires Docker is a gate that lies. Tier 2 remains runnable and is where the database tests belong.

coveragePreservation.rule: Every test file must be REACHABLE, EXPLICITLY RETIRED, or EXPLICITLY QUARANTINED. No silent orphaning.
